meaning: A stranger, or someone who is completely unaware or oblivious.
cultural_vibe: In Marwari households, being 'ajaano' often carries a touch of affectionate teasing, used for someone pretending ignorance or a newcomer finding their roots.
dialogue_marwari: ए दाई! नयो मेहमान आया पछि यूँ अजाणो क्यूं बण रीयो है? बैठो, म्हासे बात करो!
dialogue_english: Hey elder brother! Why are you acting like a stranger after the new guest arrived? Sit down and talk to us!
family_prompt: Who in the family always acts 'ajaano' when it's their turn to do the household chores?

theme: Kitchen, Food & Street Snacks (Ransoi, Chatkara & Mitthan)
meaning: Traditional sweet broken-wheat dessert cooked in ghee and jaggery, made on auspicious occasions.
cultural_vibe: No Marwari celebration—be it a wedding, festival, or child's birth—is complete without the sweet aroma of freshly churned Laapsi served with oodles of desi ghee.
dialogue_marwari: अरे बासा, आज घर में कूंणसो खास हुयो है? रसोड़े सूं तो लापसी की गऊ महक आवे!
dialogue_english: Oh elders, what special occasion is at home today? The wonderful aroma of Laapsi is wafting from the kitchen!
family_prompt: Who in your family makes the best traditional Laapsi with extra ghee? Drop a heart for your favorite chef!

theme: Vintage Artifacts & Sunday Wisdom (Ghar Ri Cheezan & Gyan)
meaning: Traditional Rajasthani amulet neck pendant shaped like a drum.
cultural_vibe: Handcrafted in silver, the Mandaliyo was traditionally worn by women as a symbol of marital grace and protection, echoing the rhythm of folk heritage.
dialogue_marwari: दादी: बेटा, ई पुराने बक्से में म्हारो चांदी रो मांदळियो पड़यो है, आज फेर पैरवू के?
dialogue_english: Grandmother: Son, my silver Mandaliyo is lying in this old box; should I wear it today?
family_prompt: Does anyone in the family still have our ancestral silver jewelry preserved? Share a photo if you find it!

meaning: A restless soul who cannot sit still for a single moment.
cultural_vibe: In Marwari households, boundless energy is often affectionately (and playfully) blamed on having quicksilver in one's heels.
dialogue_marwari: अरे बैठ जाइजे थारी जगह! कंठोई चैन कोनी, बातां ई बातां में दस फेरा काट आया। कूट-कूट'र अळपम्पो भरियो है थारै मा रै!
dialogue_english: Will you sit down in one place! You have no peace; walking around ten times while talking. You are packed to the brim with restlessness!
family_prompt: Who is the biggest 'Alpampo' in our family who simply cannot sit in one place during Sunday family calls?

meaning: Wait and see which way the result lands.
cultural_vibe: Born from the desert landscape where camels sit resting on one side or the other, symbolizing unpredictable outcomes.
dialogue_marwari: चुनाव रा परिणाम आय रिया है, रुको ज़रा, देखस्यां ऊँट किस करवट बैठता है!
dialogue_english: Election results are coming, wait a minute, let's see which way the camel sits!
family_prompt: What's a major decision or result you are currently waiting on in suspense?

meaning: A grand traditional feast hosted by the groom's family for the bride's relatives.
cultural_vibe: Rooted in Marwari hospitality (Mehmaan-nawazi), this pre-wedding feast strengthens ties between two families through royal-style community dining and joyous celebration.
dialogue_marwari: अरे बन्ना सा, ब्याव में साजन-गोठ कौंणसूं दिन राखड़ी है? सगळा मेहमान पैलांई पूछ रिया है!
dialogue_english: Hey groom-to-be, on which day have you kept the Saajan-Goth feast for the wedding? All the guests are asking in advance!
family_prompt: What is your absolute favorite traditional delicacy you always look forward to eating at a grand Marwari Saajan-Goth?

meaning: A sharp sarcastic jibe or taunt often used playfully by elders.
cultural_vibe: In Marwari households, a 'mehno' is an art form—half complaint, half affection. It's how elders lovingly keep the young ones in check with a smile.
dialogue_marwari: अरे छोरा! इत्ता दिन होग्या फोन कोनी करियो, अब कैया याद आई म्हारी?
dialogue_english: Oh son! It's been ages since you called, how did you remember me today?
family_prompt: What's the funniest 'mehno' your dadi or nani has ever thrown at you?

meaning: A sweet, reproachful complaint for not visiting or calling.
cultural_vibe: Rooted in Marwari hospitality, 'Olbho' captures the gentle grievance of elders missing their loved ones.
dialogue_marwari: अरे बन्ना! दो महिना होइग्या, थाने कदै याद ई कोनी आई? थारो ओळभो करणो पड़सी अब तो!
dialogue_english: Hey dear! It's been two months, didn't you even remember us? Now we must lodge a sweet complaint (olbho) against you!
family_prompt: Who in the family do you owe an 'olbho' to for not calling this week? Tag them below!

theme: Kitchen, Food & Street Snacks (Ransoi, Chatkara & Mitthan)
meaning: Thick, crisp pearl millet (bajra) flatbread served generously with white butter.
cultural_vibe: The undisputed king of Marwari winter tables, traditionally paired with lasun ki chutney and fresh white butter to keep the desert chill at bay.
dialogue_marwari: अरे छोरा, बाजरे को गरम सोगरो ल्याऊं के ऊपर देसी घी चूपड़'र?
dialogue_english: Hey son, shall I bring a hot bajra sogro drenched in homemade ghee?
family_prompt: Who in our family makes the crispiest sogro, and do you prefer it with gur (jaggery) or lehsun ki chutney?

meaning: Festive songs and celebratory rituals sung during auspicious family occasions.
cultural_vibe: In Marwar, every joyful milestone—from weddings to the birth of a child—begins with women gathering to sing folk songs called 'badhaavo', filling the haveli with blessings.
dialogue_marwari: घरे बधावो बाज रिया है, बेटा! जल्दी तैयार हो जाओ, मेहमान आर्या है।
dialogue_english: The celebratory songs are playing at home, son! Get ready quickly, the guests have arrived.
family_prompt: Dada-Dadi, which traditional 'badhaavo' song is your absolute favorite to sing during family weddings?
